Allergic contact dermatitis is plausible if exposure occurred on the thigh (e.g., new clothing, lotion) and spread via scratching or secondary sensitization; however, bilateral/upper limb involvement without clear exposure history makes it slightly less likely. Atopic dermatitis flare is considered given generalized pruritus and papular morphology, but the abrupt onset and lack of chronic eczematous features (e.g., lichenification, xerosis) reduce confidence. Tinea corporis is lower-confidence: while it can cause annular, scaly plaques with peripheral papules, isolated pruritic papules without scale, central clearing, or lymphangitic spread are atypical—and rapid spread to non-contiguous sites (left leg, forearm) is unusual without autoinoculation or immune compromise."}
